t: Timur rose from a minor Barlas noble to master of the western Chagatai Khanate by about 1370 and spent the next 35 years at war, defeating the Golden Horde, the Delhi Sultanate, the Mamluks and the Ottomans.
His campaigns relied on terror: Isfahan, Delhi, Baghdad and Damascus were massacred, and scholars estimate that his wars caused the deaths of millions of people.
He enriched Samarkand and patronised scholars and poets, but his empire fragmented soon after his death; his descendants included Ulugh Beg and Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire.
dyk: Timur's nickname, Temur-i Lang, 'Timur the Lame', from injuries to his right leg and hand, is the origin of the Western name Tamerlane; a Soviet examination of his remains in 1941 confirmed the injuries.
ev: Timur defeats his rival Amir Husayn and is proclaimed sovereign at Balkh
Timur begins his conquest of Persia with the destruction of Herat
After a revolt, Timur orders the massacre of the people of Isfahan
Timur defeats Tokhtamysh at the Battle of the Terek River
Timur invades northern India and sacks Delhi
Timur's armies sack Damascus and Baghdad
Timur defeats and captures the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I at the Battle of Ankara
Timur dies at Farab on campaign against Ming China

f.born: in the 1320s, near Kesh (now Shahrisabz, Uzbekistan) in the Chagatai Khanate; son of Taraghai, a noble of the Turkicised Mongol Barlas tribe; later Timurid histories give 8 April 1336
f.died: 17 or 18 February 1405, at Farab beyond the Syr Darya, of illness during a winter campaign against Ming China; buried in the Gur-e-Amir, Samarkand
f.role: Chief of the Barlas from about 1360; sovereign at Balkh from about 1370, ruling as amir and güregen (royal son-in-law) in the name of puppet Chagatayid khans; styled Sahib Qiran, 'Lord of the Conjunction'
f.known: founding the Timurid Empire; wars with Tokhtamysh and the Golden Horde; the sack of Delhi (1398); the sacks of Isfahan, Baghdad, Aleppo and Damascus; the defeat of Bayezid I at Ankara (1402); patronage of Samarkand and of scholars; the Timurid Renaissance
